title: Principal fixed-rank bases for a finite locally free affine algebra
statement:
Let $A,B$ be commutative rings and $\varphi:A\to B$ a unital homomorphism. Let $p:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be finite locally free of degree $r\ge0$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and put $E=p_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$. Then $E$ is a quasi-coherent module locally free of constant rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. There exist $m\ge0$, elements $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in A$ with $(f_1,\ldots,f_m)=A$, and bases $e_{i,1},\ldots,e_{i,r}$ of the $A_{f_i}$-modules $B_{f_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Here $B_{f_i}$ means localization as an $A$-module, with the induced algebra structure, equivalently $B[1/\varphi(f_i)]$. For each $i$, the canonical maps
$$A_{f_i}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}(D(f_i)),\qquad B_{f_i}\longrightarrow E(D(f_i)),\qquad t/f_i^n\longmapsto(f_i|_{D(f_i)})^{-n}t|_{D(f_i)}$$
are respectively a ring isomorphism and a compatible module isomorphism. Under these maps the chosen basis identifies $E|_{D(f_i)}$ with $\mathcal O_{D(f_i)}^{\oplus r}$. If $A\ne0$, the family can be chosen with all $D(f_i)$ nonempty; if $A=0$, then $B=0$ and the empty family is allowed. No Noetherian or global freeness assumption is made.

source.place: Tags 02KB (morphisms-lemma-finite-flat), 04MH (morphisms-lemma-finite-locally-free), and 01IA (schemes-lemma-quasi-coherent-affine); finite principal refinement and localization of sections in old item proof steps 2-3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-flf-properties] to $p$ and degree $r$. It gives that $E$ is locally free of rank $r$. By [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], $E$ is quasi-coherent and has an open cover $(V_a)$ with trivializations $\theta_a:\mathcal O_{V_a}^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{\sim}E|_{V_a}$. The degree hypothesis is exactly the fibre-dimension hypothesis in [def-pc-finite-locally-free]; no Noetherian assumption is used.

For every f in A, use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b) on Spec A to obtain the canonical ring isomorphism A_f ≅ O(D(f)). The inverse image of D(f) under Spec(φ) is D(φ(f)) in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Its structure-sheaf sections are the localization of B at φ(f), again by the same basic-open structure-sheaf localization result. Regard this localization as an A-module localization: invertibility, denominator clearing and the equality criterion restrict along φ, so its canonical map from B is an A-module localization at f in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. The universal property gives B_f ≅ E(D(f)), and separately B_f ≅ B[1/φ(f)] in [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. The ring structure is preserved because fractions multiply by multiplying numerators and denominators. Compatibility of Spec(φ) with constant sections identifies the scalar structures; uniqueness of extension of scalars to A_f makes the section equivalence A_f-linear. Finally t/f^n = f^{-n}·(t/1), giving both required fraction formulas. This direct structure-sheaf argument does not use generic quasi-coherent module localization.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), clauses (1), (3), (5); elementary restriction of the localization universal property along A → B and extension of scalars.

proof.text: For each $x\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, choose $V_a$ containing $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](i), choose $f_x$ with $x\in D(f_x)\subseteq V_a$. These nonempty principal opens cover the spectrum. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](iii), finitely many suffice, say $D(f_1),\ldots,D(f_m)$; its assertion (i) gives $(f_1,\ldots,f_m)=A$. Each retains its restricted trivialization $\theta_i$. This also works for the empty spectrum by choosing no opens. More explicitly, if $A=0$, unitality gives $1_B=\varphi(1_A)=\varphi(0)=0$, hence $B=0$; there are no prime ideals in $A$, and the empty family generates its unit ideal. If $A\ne0$, the chosen opens are all nonempty because each contains its chosen point. In Lean, restrict each sheaf isomorphism along the inclusion D(f) → V using overMap, which preserves the unit and free coproducts. Index the initial cover by points, and reindex the finite subcover by Fin m. If A is the zero ring, its spectrum and hence the selected finite set of points are empty.

For each retained $i$, restrict $\theta_i$ to global sections on $D(f_i)$, and let $e_{i,j}\in B_{f_i}$ be the inverse image of $\theta_i(\delta_j)$ under the module isomorphism of step 2. Here $\delta_j$ is the $j$th standard coordinate section of $\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$. A finite direct sum has section module $\mathcal O(D(f_i))^r$: coordinates and their inverse are defined sectionwise. Thus, using the ring isomorphism of step 2, this is an $A_{f_i}$-linear isomorphism $A_{f_i}^r\cong B_{f_i}$, whose standard basis maps to $(e_{i,1},\ldots,e_{i,r})$, a basis in [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. On every subopen $W\subseteq D(f_i)$ the original trivialization sends $(a_j)$ to $\sum_j a_j\theta_i(\delta_j)|_W$, by linearity; hence it is exactly the sheaf identification induced by these basis sections and the canonical localization maps. For $r=0$ the sums and bases are empty and the same maps identify $E|_{D(f_i)}$ with the zero module sheaf. Concretely, freeSectionsLinearEquiv gives the section coordinates; map the standard basis through the inverse coordinate equivalence, change coefficients along A_f ≅ O(D(f)), and then transport through the inverse canonical module equivalence. The equation on each coordinate generator follows from the free projection-inclusion identities.

Step 2: section-vanishing-prime(b) on U=X=Spec A gives A_f≅O(D(f)). basic-open-localization (1) gives surjectivity of t/f^n↦f^{-n}t| and (2) gives injectivity. Well-definedness, A_f-linearity and B_f≅B[1/φ(f)] follow in a few lines, so elementary is justified. Step 3: basis clause (i), quasi-compactness (iii) and the unit-ideal clause (i) give the finite cover; each D(f_i) is nonempty because it contains its chosen point; A=0 forces B=0 and the empty family. Step 4: coordinates of θ_i on D(f_i) give an A_f-iso A_f^r≅B_f, and by linearity it induces the sheaf trivialization. Edge cases checked: A=0, r=0 with A≠0 (B=0, empty bases), disconnected A, nilpotents; no Noetherian hypothesis is used.
